options.name: Control mapping against the enterprise framework with manual evidence
options.summary: Applicable controls are mapped to the enterprise control framework. Evidence is assembled by hand at assessment time. Exceptions are recorded in the standard register.
checklist: applicable regimes identified and confirmed with compliance rather than assumed by architecture
control-to-requirement mapping complete with a named evidence source per control
exceptions and waivers registered with an owner and an expiry
residual-risk decision owner named for each position taken under uncertainty
evidence sources confirmed to exist rather than being planned

questions.question: Which positions are decisions under uncertainty needing a named owner rather than a control?
For each mapped control, does the named evidence source exist today, or is it a build dependency?
Which regimes apply that architecture has not considered - conduct, resolution, sanctions, records?

risks.statement: Manual evidence assembled at assessment time is a point-in-time claim; it says nothing about whether the control operated between assessments, which is what supervisors increasingly ask.
risks.mitigation: Automate evidence for the controls most likely to be tested, even if the rest stays manual.

risks.statement: Evidence collection consumes delivery-team effort at exactly the moments the programme is under most pressure.
risks.mitigation: Pin the person-day anchor so the recurring cost is visible in the plan rather than absorbed silently.

risks.statement: Exceptions without expiry become permanent, and the register stops representing the actual risk position.
risks.mitigation: Require an expiry on every entry and re-approval at a named forum to renew.

lld_notes: Publish the control map with, for every control, the requirement it satisfies, its evidence source and whether that source exists today.
hld_notes: The applicable regimes belong on the HLD as constraints, because they bound the design rather than describing it.

options.name: Regulatory spine with automated evidence and third-party regime coverage
options.summary: Controls are mapped to the full applicable regulatory spine. Evidence is produced by the pipeline rather than collected by hand. Third parties are assessed against the outsourcing and operational-resilience regimes with exit plans.
checklist: full regime set mapped: prudential and conduct, operational resilience, payment card, information security and data protection as applicable
control-to-requirement mapping with an automated evidence source per control where one is possible
evidence produced continuously and retained to the regulatory floor
third parties assessed for materiality and criticality with exit plans
important business services identified with impact tolerances stated
exception register with owners and expiries, reported at a named forum
residual-risk acceptances recorded with the accepting owner and the forum that accepted

questions.question: Which third parties trip the critical-third-party thresholds, and has compliance confirmed that rather than architecture assuming it?
Is this scope part of an important business service, and if so what impact tolerance applies and does the resilience position meet it?
Which controls have no automatable evidence source, and is manual collection sustainable for those?
Who accepts residual risk for this initiative, at which forum, and have they seen the register?

risks.statement: An impact tolerance stated by the business but not achievable by the resilience position is a documented gap between what was promised to a supervisor and what the architecture delivers.
risks.mitigation: Reconcile the tolerance against the measured RTO before the position is submitted, and escalate the gap rather than restating the tolerance.

risks.statement: Regulatory interpretation questions depend on compliance and sometimes on supervisory engagement, both of which run on their own timescales.
risks.mitigation: Raise interpretation questions in the first weeks and track them as dated external dependencies.

risks.statement: Automated evidence that captures configuration rather than operation proves the control was configured, not that it worked.
risks.mitigation: Capture operational evidence - the control firing - for the controls most likely to be tested.

risks.statement: Evidence automation is a build cost that recurs whenever an upstream system changes its output format.
risks.mitigation: Treat evidence collectors as production code with owners, and include them in change impact assessment.

lld_notes: Publish the control map with the automated evidence source, the collection frequency and the retention per control.
Record the impact tolerance alongside the measured RTO so the gap, if any, is visible in one place.
hld_notes: Regulatory constraints and the impact tolerance are stated on the HLD as design bounds, with the resilience position measured against them.

options.name: Full regulatory spine with model-risk governance and defensible scoring
options.summary: As the regulatory spine option, plus model-risk governance where models or LLMs are in scope: tiering, decomposable scoring, validation, and a defence of the framework's own judgements under model-risk challenge.
checklist: models in scope inventoried and tiered by materiality of the decisions they influence
model validation defined per tier, independent of the model's builder
scoring and judgements decomposable - every score traceable to its inputs and its weighting
model inputs, outputs and drift monitored with an owner for the findings
training and inference data classified and its provenance recorded
human oversight defined per model tier, with the decisions a human must take
the framework's own automated judgements treated as a model where they influence material decisions

questions.question: Which decisions do models influence, and at what materiality - does any model tier require independent validation?
Can every score this framework produces be decomposed to its inputs and weights, and defended under challenge?
What data trained or grounds the model, is its provenance recorded, and does its classification permit that use?
Where a model influences a customer outcome, what human oversight exists and is it substantive rather than nominal?

risks.statement: A scoring or prioritisation output that cannot be decomposed to its inputs and weights fails model-risk challenge, and the failure invalidates decisions already taken on the basis of those scores.
risks.mitigation: Keep every score decomposable by construction, record the weights as versioned configuration, and retain the inputs alongside the output.

risks.statement: Using production data to train or ground a model is a processing purpose that the original collection basis may not cover.
risks.mitigation: Confirm the lawful basis for the specific use before build, not after, and record the assessment.

risks.statement: Models reachable from an untrusted input path can be manipulated through their inputs, and the manipulation is invisible in conventional application telemetry.
risks.mitigation: Treat model inputs as untrusted at every boundary, constrain what a model output is permitted to trigger, and log inference with the same weight as any other privileged action.

risks.statement: Independent model validation is a queue outside the programme's control and is frequently the last gate before go-live.
risks.mitigation: Book validation capacity when the model tier is first known, not when the model is finished.

risks.statement: Model drift monitoring produces findings that need an owner with authority to withdraw a model from service.
risks.mitigation: Name that owner and agree the withdrawal threshold before deployment.

lld_notes: Record per model: purpose, tier, inputs, training or grounding data with provenance, validation status and drift monitoring.
Publish the scoring decomposition for any automated judgement that influences a material decision, this framework's own outputs included.
hld_notes: Models appear on the e2e flow with their input trust boundaries marked, because the input path is the attack surface.
